body.statement:
Open-ended Question 6. Put \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\). For every sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\), determine the epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit, in the weak topology, of the rescaled design-profile risks \(J^{4/3}\{\mathsf R_J-1/(2J)\}\) specified by the second-order pair-orbit selection handle \(\mathcal L_{(s_J)}\), and use its exact contact conditions to characterize \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\). At \(\rho=1/2\) and finite \(\kappa=\lim_J\kappa_J\), prove or refute a matching lower expansion for the candidate upper-bound functional
\[
 \mu\longmapsto
 \mathcal A(\mu)+\kappa\left(2\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
 \qquad \mu\in\mathcal F_{1/2},
\]
where \(\mathcal A\) is to be derived from the unrestricted Airy/local pair-orbit experiment. Treat \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) as the distinct one-sided, recentered, and tangent regimes specified in the handle. A complete answer must prove uniform lower and recovery expansions and must recover the proposed contact points by exact finite minimizers. The displayed hard-budget term is presently only upper-bound evidence; finite-grid calculations do not establish the asserted limit or exact-minimizer recovery.
body.justification: Exact finite optimizers may select a strict subset of the flat first-order face; the corrected question identifies the \(J^{2/3}\) critical budget scale on which that selection can first interact with the unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) correction.
body.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 supplies an unrestricted scalar Airy expansion, but no published result supplies the measure-valued pair-orbit epi-limit, the boundary-uniform hard-budget lower expansion, or exact-minimizer recovery required here.
body.consumer: The answer would identify which first-order-equivalent assignment laws are limits of exact finite minimax choices along each sensitivity path and would provide the design analyst's smaller-order tie-breaker.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove a matching second-order lower expansion and an epi- or \(\Gamma\)-convergence theorem for the finite design-profile risks, identify the resulting contact set in each of the finite-\(\kappa\), \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) regimes, and prove that precisely those contacts are limits of exact finite minimizers.
obligation.obstruction: Theorem 5 controls risk only up to \(o(J^{-1})\), whereas selection on the proposed scale requires uniform \(J^{-4/3}\) expansions over interior and boundary schedule faces. The exact finite certificates determine each fixed grid but provide neither a limiting local kernel nor the liminf, equicoercivity, convergence-of-minima, and exact-recovery statements needed to pass finite argmin sets to a measure-valued contact set.
obligation.attempted: The finite orbit contact systems, the scalar and two-parameter shrinking-prior lower experiments, and the balanced-orbit centered-estimator upper bound yield the exact first-order face. Expanding the known first-order information game is flat on that face. The hard-budget correction identifies the critical scale algebraically and separates the one-sided candidate domains, but no available calculation supplies its matching lower expansion or the pair-orbit analogue of the unrestricted Airy functional uniformly on all boundary faces.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact finite contact system in Theorem 1 computes every set \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s_J)\), and Theorem 5 gives the rigorous first-order statements
\[
 \mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\subseteq\mathcal F_\rho
\]
and recovery of every \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\) by invariant procedures whose excess worst risk is \(o(J^{-1})\). These conclusions do not replace those procedures by exact minimizers.

The critical scale follows algebraically from the candidate hard-budget correction. Indeed, with \(\overline m_J=\int m\,d\mu_{q_J}\),
\[
 J^{4/3}
 \frac{(2\overline m_J-1)\Delta_J}{J^2}
 =\frac{\Delta_J}{J^{2/3}}(2\overline m_J-1)
 =\kappa_J(2\overline m_J-1).
\]
Thus it competes with a \(J^{-4/3}\) unrestricted Airy correction exactly when \(\Delta_J=O(J^{2/3})\). On \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\), \(1/2\le\int m\,d\mu\le1\). Consequently the candidate hard-budget term with \(\kappa_J\to+\infty\) is finite only on \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\). If \(\kappa_J\to-\infty\), subtracting \(\Delta_J/J^2\) changes that term to
\[
 2\kappa_J\left(\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
\]
which is nonnegative and diverges off \(\int m\,d\mu=1\). For \(\rho>1/2\), the first-order face already imposes \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\); selection then depends on transverse finite-grid deviations and requires a separate tangent expansion. These are consequences of the candidate upper correction and identify the residual regimes, not a proved epi-limit.
